pr_title: release-23.2: spanconfig: correctly order updates when applying in the KVSubscriber
pr_body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #118001 on behalf of @arulajmani.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

----

Previously, there was no ordering guarantee between KVSubscriber events at the same timestamp. As a result, if a batch of events included updates to overlapping spans at the same timestamp, we could apply additions before deletions -- this would cause the additions to get clobbered, which was not the intention. This could lead to missing span configurations, resulting in bugs such as the linked issue.

This patch fixes the issue by sorting deletions before additions if two span configuration events have the same timestamp.

Closes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/110908

Release note (bug fix): Previously, altering from a Regional By Row table to a Regional By Table table could cause leaseholders to never move to the databse's primary region. This is now fixed.

----

Release justification: low risk, high benefit bug fix.

issue_context.title: spanconfig: incorrect span config after switching to from regional by row to regional by table
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

After converting a system from regional by row to regional by table, there are keys in the `spanConfigStore` that return an error on `getSpanConfigForKey`. Specifically, keys at range boundaries of the old regional by row tables. This prevents various KV queues from working on these ranges.

**To Reproduce**

```sql
cockroach demo --nodes=3 --demo-locality=region=us-east1,zone=a:region=us-central1,zone=a:region=us-west1,zone=a --empty --multitenant=false --log-dir=/tmp/logs

-- Prevent the ranges from merging back - on a real cluster they may or may not merge based on data in adjacent ranges
 SET CLUSTER SETTING kv.range_merge.queue_enabled=false;

alter database defaultdb set primary region 'us-east1';
alter database defaultdb add region 'us-central1';
alter database defaultdb add region 'us-west1';

-- create regional by table
create table t (i int primary key);
select start_key, end_key, range_id, lease_holder from [show ranges from table t with details];
   start_key   |   end_key    | range_id | lease_holder
---------------+--------------+----------+---------------
  …/<TableMin> | <after:/Max> |       65 |            1

-- alter to regional by row
alter table t set locality regional by row;
-- wait a few seconds...
select start_key, end_key, range_id, lease_holder from [show ranges from table t with details];
       start_key       |       end_key        | range_id | lease_holder
-----------------------+----------------------+----------+---------------
  …/<TableMin>         | …/2                  |       65 |            1
  …/2                  | …/2/"@"              |       66 |            1
  …/2/"@"              | …/2/"@"/PrefixEnd    |       67 |            2
  …/2/"@"/PrefixEnd    | …/2/"\xc0"           |       68 |            1
  …/2/"\xc0"           | …/2/"\xc0"/PrefixEnd |       69 |            3
  …/2/"\xc0"/PrefixEnd | <after:/Max>         |       70 |            1

-- alter back to regional by table
alter table t set locality regional by table;
select start_key, end_key, range_id, lease_holder from [show ranges from table t with details];
                             ->
       start_key       |       end_key        | range_id | lease_holder
-----------------------+----------------------+----------+---------------
  …/<TableMin>         | …/2                  |       65 |            1
  …/2                  | …/2/"@"              |       66 |            1
  …/2/"@"              | …/2/"@"/PrefixEnd    |       67 |            2
  …/2/"@"/PrefixEnd    | …/2/"\xc0"           |       68 |            1
  …/2/"\xc0"           | …/2/"\xc0"/PrefixEnd |       69 |            3
  …/2/"\xc0"/PrefixEnd | …/4                  |       70 |            1
  …/4                  | <after:/Max>         |       71 |            1

-- manually enqueue a range and look at the logs
 select crdb_internal.kv_enqueue_replica(70, 'replicate', true);
```
From the log after enqueing all the ranges on n1
```
W230919 15:53:50.293293 9623 spanconfig/spanconfigstore/span_store.go:239 ⋮ [T1,Vsystem,n1,client=127.0.0.1:60377,hostssl,user=‹demo›,s1,r70/1:‹/Table/106/{2/"\xc0…-4}›] 6984  span config not found for ‹/Table/106/2/"\xc0"/PrefixEnd›
W230919 15:54:32.634871 9623 spanconfig/spanconfigstore/span_store.go:239 ⋮ [T1,Vsystem,n1,client=127.0.0.1:60377,hostssl,user=‹demo›,s1,r71/1:‹/{Table/106/4-Max}›] 7025  span config not found for ‹/Table/106/4›
W230919 15:55:39.371312 9623 spanconfig/spanconfigstore/span_store.go:239 ⋮ [T1,Vsystem,n1,client=127.0.0.1:60377,hostssl,user=‹demo›,s1,r68/1:‹/Table/106/2/"{@"/Pr…-\xc0"}›] 7109  span config not found for ‹/Table/106/2/"@"/PrefixEnd›
```

If the ranges are merged because the left hand neighbor of the range is small enough, then it may merge away, but this is not guaranteed to ever happen

**Expected behavior**
A span config is expected to be returned for all ranges. This should then adjust the leases for these ranges to the correct place.


Jira issue: CRDB-31671

gz#18665

Epic CRDB-32846
comments:
There is a "workaround" to this problem which requires a minor change to any field in the zone config for the table. For instance running:
`alter database defaultdb CONFIGURE ZONE USING gc.ttlseconds = 14401;`
after this issue will fix the span config cache and subsequently the ranges will be correctly moved to the correct leaseholder.

From Slack:

> could it be that we're applying the updates in the wrong order to the store? Around here: [https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/88e8fc80afda96df6710324c7ba2c1887176ca21/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigkvsubscriber/kvsubscriber.go#L4[…]49](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/88e8fc80afda96df6710324c7ba2c1887176ca21/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigkvsubscriber/kvsubscriber.go#L444-L449)?

It was indeed this.

review_comments: Should we have added `Deletion() bool` to the `rangefeedbuffer.Event` interface?
Were you also suggesting we include `Deletion() bool` in `rangefeedbuffer.Flush` instead of building this additional sorting on top over here?

I wasn't suggesting that, but since you brought it up, should we do that?

To me (someone not particularly familiar with this package), it seems off for this `handlePartialUpdate` function to operate on `rangefeedbuffer.Event` interfaces, but then to assume that they are always `*BufferEvent` instances. I now see that we're also doing this later in the function though, so I guess this is nothing new. So we don't need to hold up this backport on this.

Maybe what I'm missing is that these `*BufferEvent` instances are coming from the same `spanconfigkvsubscriber` package, and are only passing through an interface before being handed back to `spanconfigkvsubscriber`. So what we really want is to parameterize our use of the `rangefeedcache` package with our `Event` type. Something like https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/119870.

> I wasn't suggesting that, but since you brought it up, should we do that?

I considered this initially, but then chose not to change any of the other users of `rangefeedbuffer` in favour of keeping this change targeted. We could revisit this, but with your cleanup in #119870, I think it's fine. Thanks for sending that out btw! 

I'll merge this once CI is happy.
